facts.text: Oud Metha, also called Al Nasr, takes its name from the Arabic 'عود ميثاء', meaning 'The Victory', reflecting early residents' hopes.
During the 1960s and 1970s, Oud Metha became a key settlement spot as expatriates flocked to Dubai's growing trade and oil boom.
The Dubai Metro's Green Line serves Oud Metha with a dedicated station, linking the area directly to downtown and the airport.
Al-Nasr Sports Club, founded in 1970, plays in the UAE League and is headquartered in Oud Metha.
Lycée Français International Georges Pompidou operates a preschool campus in Oud Metha, offering French curriculum to local families.
Situated at roughly 25°14′15″N 55°18′42″E, Oud Metha lies on Dubai Creek's western bank, overlooking historic waterfronts.
